title: Training Notes — Returned-Payment Fees in a Replacement Payment, Patient Financial Account
content:
**Rule taught.** The returned-payment fees a returned-payment replacement on the Patient Financial Account includes depend on the fees posted:

- when two or more returned payment fee charges were posted in the 12 calendar months before the handling date, every one of them is included;
- when exactly one was posted in those 12 months and the account holds a card on file, no fee is included, and the fee stays on the account for the ordinary statement;
- otherwise, no different fee treatment applies under this rule.

A window of calendar months for the returned-payment replacement ends on the handling date and reaches back that many months, a date on the same calendar day that many months earlier falling outside it. A returned payment fee charge counts by its posting date. "Holds a card on file" is what the account record shows about a card kept on file.

## Questions from training

**Q. Two fees of 30.00 in the last 12 months.** Both are included: 60.00 of fees.

**Q. Three fees in the last 12 months.** All three are included.

**Q. One fee of 30.00 in the last 12 months, and the account holds a card on file.** No fee is included; the 30.00 stays on the account for the ordinary statement.

**Q. A fee posted on 7 May 2025, handling date 7 May 2026.** It falls outside the 12 months, since the same calendar day 12 months earlier is outside the window.

| Returned payment fee charges posted in the 12 months | Card on file held | Fees included |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | any | every one of them |
| exactly 1 | yes | none; the fee stays for the ordinary statement |
| exactly 1 | no | no different treatment under this rule |
| 0 | any | no different treatment under this rule |
